old_title: Ukraine live: Trump's envoys confronted over holding talks with 'war criminal' Putin
new_title: Ukraine war live: Zelensky says Moscow tried to kill as many people in Kyiv attack
old_text:
Donald Trump's peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have been confronted over their talks with "war criminal" Russian president Vladimir Putin.
In a news conference in Kyiv alongside Volodymry Zelensky on Sunday, Ukrainian journalist Dmytro Gordon asked whether Putin was deceiving the US president.
"You have met with President Putin very often. Does it seem to you that Putin has been deceiving you all this time?," he added according to the Kyiv Post.
"And finally, don't you find it disgusting to sit at the same table with an international war criminal, the executioner of the Ukrainian people, who is personally responsible for the tragedy in Ukraine?" he added.
Zelensky held talks with Witkoff and Kushner on Sunday, after their three-hour talks with Putin in Moscow on Saturday. He lauded their "very substantive" conversation and said Ukraine was ready for trilateral talks involving Russia, the US and Ukraine.
The US president is expected to speak to Putin and Zelensky over the phone on Monday.
Meanwhile, Kyiv's air raid alerts have reached their highest level since the war began in February 2022, as Russia ramps up its targeting of the Ukrainian capital, according to an analysis of government figures by BBC Verify.
Putin meets with Kushner and Witkoff amid Ukraine war peace talks - ICYMI
Zelensky says oil refinery hit in Ryazan region
Volodymyr Zelensky has said a Russian oil refinery in the Ryazan region was struck by Ukrainian drones in a fresh long-range attack.
"Our warriors continue responding justly to Russian strikes on Ukraine. An oil refinery was hit in the Ryazan region," the Ukrainian president said, sharing footage which he said was of the strike.
"Our long-range capabilities were used against oil-processing facilities in the Perm region and Tatarstan, and against a site used to store and launch attack drones in the Kursk region," he added.
"A target was also hit in the Black Sea. I thank every one of our units for their precision!"
Kyiv air raid alerts hit record high - report
Air raid alerts in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv are at their highest levels of the war so far, as Russia ramps up attacks on the Ukrainian capital, according to a report.
Moscow's new strategy of increasing daytime attacks on the city has forced it to drive up the frequency of its daily air raid alerts, BBC Verify reported in an analysis of Ukrainian government figures.
Residents have been forced to head to the shelters as often as 13 times a day, the analysis said.
'Overnight we all became war correspondents': Ukraine's local newspapers face battle to stay alive
In the weeks leading up to Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine, the headlines in a Kyiv newspaper looked much like they would anywhere else.
There was some debate over whether Russia would actually attack its neighbour. But then, outside of politics, there was everything else: the tourists stuck abroad, changes to school meals and the spread of the Omicron variant of Covid.
On 24 February 2022, everything changed as Russian tanks rolled across the border. Businesses closed or relocated, martial law saw hundreds of thousands of working-age men recruited for military service, and around one million people fled the country in the first week.
A brave few stayed behind to keep a record of what happened as the missiles rained down. Local journalists observed and asked questions as their communities were torn apart by the war.
Industrial facility damaged in Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Tatarstan region
An industrial facility sustained minor damage in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Tatarstan region on the Volga river, the state-run TASS news agency reported on Monday, citing the regional governor's press service.
The news agency has not identified the facility or specified its location.
Eleven dead and six missing after avalanche in Russian mountains
The avalanche hit a group of climbers in the Kabardino-Balkaria region in the North Caucasus on Sunday.
It swept down Mount Mizhirgi, one of the area's highest peaks, around 5pm local time (2pm GMT), hitting a group of 33 climbers, emergency services said.
Ten climbers had made their own way down the mountain as of 9am local time on Monday.
Russia launches 92 drones at Ukraine, says Kyiv's air force
Russian forces have attacked Ukraine with 92 drones overnight into Monday, the Ukrainian air force has said in its daily update.
Kyiv's air force shot down or jammed 71 of the drones, while 12 locations were struck, it said.
Aircraft, anti-aircraft missile units, and electronic warfare was used to down the drones, the force said in the Telegram update.
As of 7am BST it said the attack was ongoing.
Trump to speak with Putin and Zelensky on Monday
Donald Trump is set to hold phone calls with Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday, according to a report.
The US president will first speak with the Russian president before speaking to Mr Zelensky, after he is briefed by his envoys on their latest talks with Russian and Ukrainian negotiators, a report in The Kyiv Independent said.
The US envoys arrived in Kyiv by train on 6 September where they were met by Mr Zelensky at Sofiiska Square, before they engaged in negotiations.
Russia and North Korea open new bridge over Tumen river
North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge on Monday, Russia's TASS state news agency reported.
The structure spans the Tumen river and is located near the "Friendship Bridge", a rail bridge commissioned in 1959 after the Korean war.
There are already direct air and rail links between Moscow and Pyongyang, who have described the new bridge as yet another milestone in their growing strategic partnership.
Russian prime minister Mikhail Mishustin said the bridge should spur development between the two countries in various spheres - including tourism - and create new jobs.
"I am convinced that the expansion of cross-border transport infrastructure will provide a powerful impetus for the further development of trade, economic, scientific, technological and cultural cooperation," TASS cited Mishustin as saying at the bridge's opening ceremony via video link.
Construction of the new bridge, which had been under discussion for years, began in April last year after its construction was agreed during a visit by President Vladimir Putin to North Korea in 2024.
The two countries' ties have grown stronger since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022 with Pyongyang sending thousands of troops to Russia's Kursk region to help repel a 2024 Ukrainian incursion there.
new_text:
Volodymyr Zelensky has accused Russia of trying to "cause as much harm to life as possible", in its latest missile and drone attack on Kyiv that has killed at least two.
"It was a complex attack that the Russians tried to plan to cause as much harm to life as possible - ballistic missiles, cruise and anti-ship missiles, and jet-powered 'shaheds'," the Ukrainian president wrote on X.
"There is significant damage to residential buildings and other civilian infrastructure in the capital."
Kyiv's mayor Vitali Klitschko said 10 more had been injured in the city, while falling debris in one district caused fires at a five-storey apartment building and a three-storey residential block.
The attack damaged at least 14 high-rise buildings, a dorm, a school, a clinic, warehouses and other sites, officials said.
It came just a day after US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held peace talks with Volodymyr Zelensky and left the Ukrainian capital.
During their visit to Kyiv, Donald Trump's peace envoys were confronted over their talks with "war criminal" Russian president Vladimir Putin.
Zelensky says US negotiators brought 'decent ideas' on ending war
Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelenskiy has said that US peace negotiators have presented several "decent ideas" to be discussed during talks on how to end the war.
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited both Russia and Ukraine over the weekend.
Mr Zelensky told reporters in a WhatsApp media chat that the next trilateral meeting could be hosted by Turkey, the UAE, Switzerland, or other countries. He expected grain shipments and energy infrastructure to be discussed there, among other issues.
He said he hopes to meet Donald Trump later this month and plans to discuss a winter air defence package.
Russia has intensified its air attacks on Ukraine, with Kyiv facing a critical shortage of air defence supplies.
Moscow confident that victory over Ukraine is 'very near', says Kremlin
Russia is confident that victory in the conflict with Ukraine is "very near," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday while speaking to Indian journalists.
"Yes, we are confident, and we are sure that victory is very near," Peskov said.
Analysis | Why the AfD's German triumph is a win for Putin - and leaves Ukraine exposed
The success of Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in state elections could herald a disaster for Ukraine, a European victory for Vladimir Putin, and a stampede of greed over democracy orchestrated by one man.
Kirill Dmitriev is to Donald Trump's envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, what Putin is to the 47th president - their favourite and much favoured Russian.
What Putin gives Trump - the thrill of proximity to unlimited power - Dmitriev offers to America: unlimited potential wealth. He is the head of the Russian Direct Investment Fund, Moscow's sovereign wealth government slush pot, and he has close links to the AfD.
There was unbridled delight in Moscow with the success of the AfD over the weekend.
Dmitriev called the result a win that "humiliates the arrogance, narrow-mindedness, warmongering, ineptitude and hypocrisy" of German chancellor Friedrich Merz's governing coalition.
The AfD, seen by German intelligence as an extremist organisation, has enjoyed (among other things) Russian support for its social media campaigns to win the elections in Saxony-Anhalt, according to German and other European intelligence sources.
Poland activates aircraft and suspends flights amid Russian missile attacks on Ukraine
Poland has launched preventive operations against Russian missile attacks on Ukraine, the Polish army has said.
The NATO and European Union member temporarily suspended flights at Lublin airport because of the military operations.
It has suffered repeated drone and plane incursions by Russia over the past year.
UK commits £100mil air defence package for Ukraine, including Patriot missiles
The UK is set to provide a £100 million air defence package for Ukraine ahead of the winter, including Patriot missiles, the government has announced.
Weapons will be provided through the PURL initiative, in which European countries buy American weapons and provide them to Ukraine
"Both the Prime Minister and I heard loud and clear on our first visits to Kyiv the importance of supporting Ukraine through this winter, as Putin prepares to use winter as a weapon by continuing barbaric attacks against civilian and energy targets. We promised to mobilise allies and provide more support wherever we can," defence secretary Wes Streeting said.
The package will include patriot missiles, which are used to stoop aircraft, and cruise and ballistic missiles, along with other air defence equipment.
Two killed in Ukrainian strikes on Russian-occupied Crimea
We're getting more reports of overnight attacks coming in, this time Ukrainian strikes on the Russian-occupied Crimean peninsula.
Two people have been killed and one has been wounded in the attack, which was annexed by Russia in 2014, according to Moscow-appointed regional governor Sergei Aksyonov.
Full report: Burnham issues statement on Ukraine after holding fresh Trump talks
Prime Minister Andy Burnham and US President Donald Trump agreed on the need to "continue working towards a ceasefire that prevented more loss of life" following a fresh wave of talks, Downing Street said.
Mr Burnham spoke with Mr Trump on Monday afternoon.
It follows a visit to Kyiv on Sunday by US envoys, who held talks in an effort to end the conflict with Russia.
A Downing Street spokesperson said: "On Ukraine, the two leaders agreed on the need to continue working towards a ceasefire that prevented more loss of life.
"The Prime Minister reiterated the UK's support for Ukraine and for recent US-led peace negotiations.
"On the Middle East, the Prime Minister set out the UK's commitment to working towards peace and security in the region, stressing the importance of the Two-State Solution, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and ensuring that Iran never acquires a nuclear weapon."

Two killed and seven injured in Russian missile attack on Kyiv
Russian air strikes have killed at least two people and injured seven others in Ukraine's capital Kyiv this morning, officials said.
The attacks came just a day after US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held peace talks with Volodymyr Zelensky and left the Ukrainian capital.
People were also trapped in a residential building and there were fires across Kyiv, mayor Vitali Klitschko said, after what he said were Russian ballistic missile strikes.
Polish armed forces conclude air operation as no airspace violations recorded
Polish Air Force has ended operations related to Russian strikes on Ukraine, Polish army said on X.
"We inform you that no violations of airspace were recorded," the army said.
Hours earlier, Polish airport in Lublin resumed air operations after temporary closure due to operations of military aviation, the Polish Air Navigation Services Agency (PANSA) said.
